note: Apollo Scout. Written by the weekly scout task, read by the admin dashboard. pending = waiting for Ziyad's ✓/✗ (stored in Firestore scout/picks); done = ids already added or skipped, never suggested again.

pending.why: A tiny museum packed wall to ceiling with about 3,000 kites from Japan and around the world, from samurai faces to giant Edo-era kites. Moved in 2020 to the Muromachi NS Building (2F); only ¥220, open 11:00–17:00, closed Sundays and holidays.
An old townhouse full of Edo-period mechanical toys you're allowed to pick up and play with. Free, open 9:00–17:00, closed Wednesdays; a 10-minute walk from Nara Park.

Japan's only museum of traditional carpentry tools: about 30,000 planes, saws and chisels, and how temples are built without nails, in a calm wooden building. 3 minutes from Shin-Kobe Station; closed Mondays.
The cult Osaka select shop opened its Kyoto branch on Fuyacho-dori in August 2026: designer and street fashion, a Kyoto-only bag and tea bowls by local potters. 11:00–20:00, closed Wednesdays.
Tokyo's single-origin roaster NOZY COFFEE opened its first Kyoto shop in January 2026, in an old machiya by the Kamo River near Shijo. Open 8:00–21:00 (20:00 in winter).
pending.halal: Coffee; it also serves coffee cocktails and beer.

pending.why: A shaved-ice café on Kiyamachi by Pontocho, opened April 2026, with fluffy kakigori created by Tokyo's famous Sakanoue Cafe, plus hotcakes and cream soda. 11:00–20:30.
pending.halal: Desserts; no halal certification, so check the syrups and toppings.

pending.why: The first official Chiikawa Park shop opens 24 November 2026 on LUCUA SOUTH 11F, right on JR Osaka Station, with the park's goods all in one place. The 10F–13F character floors need a lottery or first-come ticket at first.
Bandai's figure store (S.H.Figuarts, Chogokin, Gundam and Dragon Ball figures) opens 2 December 2026 on LUCUA SOUTH 11F, its second in Japan after Akihabara.
A big food hall in Grand Green Osaka with stalls picked by Time Out, from ramen and sake to Thai and Korean. New sweets shops (Célébrité, KITAGAWA) arrive this November.
pending.halal: Mixed stalls; most aren't halal and alcohol is served.

pending.why: Halal wagyu ramen 4 minutes from Shinsaibashi Station, from the team behind a halal yakiniku place. No pork and no alcohol; soup, noodles and tare are all made halal.
pending.halal: Halal wagyu, no pork or alcohol; it says it's halal but no certificate is named, so ask in the shop.

pending.why: Said to be the oldest sweet shop in the world, open since about the year 1000 beside Imamiya Shrine. It sells one thing only: little charcoal-grilled mochi skewers in sweet white miso, eaten on tatami by the shrine path.
pending.halal: Just mochi and miso; no meat, but no halal certification.

pending.why: A free museum of Japanese ads, from Edo-era woodblock posters to award-winning TV commercials, under Caretta Shiodome. Closed Sundays and Mondays.
Artist Ken Kagami's tiny shop hidden inside an apartment building on a Daikanyama back street, full of secondhand clothes, old books and odd knickknacks he picked himself.
Kamakura's raw-chocolate brand in a whole three-storey Western-style house on Wakamiya-oji, with an open kitchen making fresh chocolate sweets on the ground floor. 10:00–18:00.
pending.halal: Chocolate and cakes; no halal certification, so check for alcohol in fillings.

pending.why: Halal wagyu ramen plus Indonesian dishes like rendang and nasi lemak, one minute from Okubo Station, with a prayer room and a rooftop. Cash only.
pending.halal: Listed as halal with a prayer room; certifying body not named, so ask in the shop.
